title.en: Ellipsis and Substitution (So do I, if so, the former, I did so)
title.es: Elipsis y sustitución (So do I, if so, the former, I did so)

text.en: Natural English does not repeat everything: it leaves out what the other person already knows (ellipsis) or replaces it with a short word (substitution). “I love jazz. So do I.” “I don’t. Neither do I.” “Which bag? The red one.” “Will it rain? I think so.” The Spanish “yo también”, “yo tampoco”, “el rojo” and “creo que sí” match this, but in English the auxiliary and the word order are fixed, and “think yes” is wrong.
text.es: El inglés natural no repite todo: omite lo que la otra persona ya sabe (elipsis) o lo reemplaza con una palabra corta (sustitución). «I love jazz. So do I.» «I don’t. Neither do I.» «Which bag? The red one.» «Will it rain? I think so.» El «yo también», el «yo tampoco», el «el rojo» y el «creo que sí» del español les corresponden, pero en inglés el auxiliar y el orden de las palabras son fijos, y «think yes» es incorrecto.

rows: puedes venir si quieres (if you want ___)

title.en: Agreeing: so and neither + auxiliary + subject
title.es: Estar de acuerdo: so y neither + auxiliar + sujeto

text.en: For a positive sentence use so, for a negative one neither (or nor). The auxiliary follows the tense of the first sentence: “I’ve seen it. So have I.” “She can swim. So can he.” If there is no auxiliary, do/does/did is used.
text.es: Para una oración afirmativa se usa so, para una negativa neither (o nor). El auxiliar sigue el tiempo de la primera oración: «I’ve seen it. So have I.» «She can swim. So can he.» Si no hay auxiliar, se usa do/does/did.

examples.es: I love jazz. So do I.

tr.en: I love jazz. So do I.
tr.es: Me encanta el jazz. A mí también.

examples.es: I don't like it. Neither do I.

tr.en: I don't like it. Neither do I.
tr.es: No me gusta. A mí tampoco.

text.en: Another form: I do too / I don’t either. After neither there is no second negative: not “neither don’t I”.
text.es: Otra forma: I do too / I don’t either. Después de neither no va una segunda negación: no «neither don’t I».

examples.es: I love jazz. I do too.

tr.en: I love jazz. I do too.
tr.es: Me encanta el jazz. A mí también.

examples.es: I don't like it. I don't either.

tr.en: I don't like it. I don't either.
tr.es: No me gusta. A mí tampoco.

title.en: One and ones: replacing a countable noun
title.es: One y ones: reemplazar un sustantivo contable

text.en: One replaces a singular countable noun, ones a plural countable noun: “Which bag? The red one.” “I prefer the green ones.” It cannot replace an uncountable noun.
text.es: One reemplaza a un sustantivo contable singular, ones a uno contable plural: «Which bag? The red one.» «I prefer the green ones.» No puede reemplazar a un sustantivo incontable.

examples.es: Which bag is yours? The red one.

tr.en: Which bag is yours? The red one.
tr.es: ¿Cuál bolsa es la tuya? La roja.

examples.es: I prefer the green ones to the blue ones.

tr.en: I prefer the green ones to the blue ones.
tr.es: Prefiero los verdes a los azules.

title.en: So and not after verbs of thinking
title.es: So y not después de verbos de pensamiento

text.en: After think, hope, suppose, believe, be afraid, so replaces the whole clause, and in the negative not or don’t think so: “I think so.” “I hope not.” “I don’t think so.” Not “I think yes”.
text.es: Después de think, hope, suppose, believe, be afraid, so reemplaza toda la cláusula, y en negativo not o don’t think so: «I think so.» «I hope not.» «I don’t think so.» No «I think yes».

examples.es: Will it rain tomorrow? I hope not.

tr.en: Will it rain tomorrow? I hope not.
tr.es: ¿Va a llover mañana? Espero que no.

examples.es: Is she coming? I think so.

tr.en: Is she coming? I think so.
tr.es: ¿Viene ella? Creo que sí.

title.en: Ellipsis after an auxiliary and the to of the infinitive
title.es: Elipsis después de un auxiliar y el to del infinitivo

text.en: After an auxiliary the repeated verb is dropped: “I haven’t finished, but my sister has.” With an infinitive the to stays: “You can stay if you want to.” “I’d love to.”
text.es: Después de un auxiliar el verbo repetido se omite: «I haven’t finished, but my sister has.» Con un infinitivo el to se queda: «You can stay if you want to.» «I’d love to.»

examples.es: I haven't finished, but my sister has.

tr.en: I haven't finished, but my sister has.
tr.es: Yo no he terminado, pero mi hermana sí.

examples.es: You can stay if you want to.

tr.en: You can stay if you want to.
tr.es: Puedes quedarte si quieres.

title.en: Another, others and ellipsis in comparisons
title.es: Another, others y la elipsis en comparaciones

text.en: Another is singular (“one more, a different one”): “I need another one.” Others is plural, without a noun: “Some like jazz and others prefer rock.” After than the auxiliary often stays: “He is taller than I am.” In place of a dropped infinitive the to stays: “I wasn’t able to.”
text.es: Another es singular («otro más, uno diferente»): «I need another one.» Others es plural, sin sustantivo: «Some like jazz and others prefer rock.» Después de than el auxiliar suele quedarse: «He is taller than I am.» En lugar de un infinitivo omitido el to se queda: «I wasn’t able to.»

examples.es: Some people like jazz and others prefer rock.

tr.en: Some people like jazz and others prefer rock.
tr.es: A algunos les gusta el jazz y a otros prefieren el rock.

examples.es: He is taller than I am.

tr.en: He is taller than I am.
tr.es: Él es más alto que yo.

title.en: Advanced ellipsis: if so, if not, the former, the latter, I would rather not
title.es: Elipsis avanzada: if so, if not, the former, the latter, I would rather not

text.en: If so means if that is the case, and if not means if it is not. So replaces the previous question or statement: “Is it ready? If so, send it. If not, call me.” I would rather not is a polite refusal: not replaces the whole verb phrase. Which she did takes over the action just mentioned: “She promised to call, which she did.”
text.es: If so significa si es así, e if not significa si no. So reemplaza la pregunta o afirmación anterior: «Is it ready? If so, send it. If not, call me.» I would rather not es un rechazo cortés: not reemplaza todo el verbo. Which she did retoma la acción mencionada: «She promised to call, which she did.»

examples.es: Is it ready? If so, send it.

tr.en: Is it ready? If so, send it.
tr.es: ¿Está listo? Si es así, mándalo.

examples.es: She promised to call, which she did.

tr.en: She promised to call, which she did.
tr.es: Prometió llamar, y lo hizo.

text.en: For two things already mentioned, the former is the first and the latter is the second: “Ann and Eva came. The former is a nurse, the latter a doctor.” After a modal the have stays and the rest is dropped: “I did not call him, but I should have.” To repeat the same action use do the same: “She ordered the soup, and I did the same.”
text.es: Para dos cosas ya mencionadas, the former es la primera y the latter la segunda: «Ann and Eva came. The former is a nurse, the latter a doctor.» Después de un modal se queda have y se omite el resto: «I did not call him, but I should have.» Para repetir la misma acción se usa do the same: «She ordered the soup, and I did the same.»

examples.es: Ann and Eva came. The former is a nurse.

tr.en: Ann and Eva came. The former is a nurse.
tr.es: Vinieron Ann y Eva. La primera es enfermera.

examples.es: I did not call him, but I should have.

tr.en: I did not call him, but I should have.
tr.es: No lo llamé, pero debí haberlo hecho.

text.en: After nor the word order is inverted, also with a modal: “I would not accept that. Nor would any sensible person.” After a conjunction the subject and be can be dropped: “When asked his name, he lied.” “If necessary, call me.”
text.es: Después de nor el orden se invierte, también con un modal: «I would not accept that. Nor would any sensible person.» Después de una conjunción se pueden omitir el sujeto y be: «When asked his name, he lied.» «If necessary, call me.»

examples.es: I would not accept that. Nor would you.

tr.en: I would not accept that. Nor would you.
tr.es: Yo no aceptaría eso. Tú tampoco.

examples.es: When asked his name, he lied.

tr.en: When asked his name, he lied.
tr.es: Cuando le preguntaron su nombre, mintió.

text.en: Spanish influence: the Spanish “yo también” is not “I too do” but “so do I” or “I do too”; “creo que sí” is not “I think yes” but “I think so”. The auxiliary must match the first sentence.
text.es: Influencia del español: el «yo también» no es «I too do» sino «so do I» o «I do too»; «creo que sí» no es «I think yes» sino «I think so». El auxiliar debe coincidir con la primera oración.

text.en: “Do so” is formal and written: “He asked me to leave, and I did so.” In speech “I did.” or “I did it.” sounds more natural.
text.es: «Do so» es formal y escrito: «He asked me to leave, and I did so.» Al hablar suena más natural «I did.» o «I did it.»

speak.en: Natural English does not repeat everything. Agreeing with a positive sentence: «I love jazz. So do I». With a negative sentence: «I don't like it. Neither do I». The auxiliary follows the tense of the first sentence: «I've seen it. So have I». «One» and «ones» replace a countable noun: «Which bag? The red one». After verbs of thinking «so» replaces the whole clause: «I think so», «I hope not». Not «I think yes».
speak.es: El inglés natural no repite todo. Estar de acuerdo con una oración afirmativa: «I love jazz. So do I». Con una negativa: «I don't like it. Neither do I». El auxiliar sigue el tiempo de la primera oración: «I've seen it. So have I». «One» y «ones» reemplazan a un sustantivo contable: «Which bag? The red one». Después de verbos de pensamiento «so» reemplaza toda la cláusula: «I think so», «I hope not». No «I think yes».

items.sentence: She promised to call, which she ___.

why.en: Which she did replaces the action just mentioned (call).
why.es: Which she did reemplaza la acción mencionada (call).

was.en: “Which she was” is not correct; the dropped verb call is replaced by did.
was.es: «Which she was» no es correcto; el verbo omitido call se reemplaza con did.

had.en: “Which she had” is not correct in this structure; you need did.
had.es: «Which she had» no es correcto en esta estructura; hace falta did.

examples: She asked me to wait, which I did.
He said he would help, which he did.

tr.en: She promised to call, which she did.
tr.es: Prometió llamar, y lo hizo.

items.sentence: Is it ready? If ___, send it to me.

why.en: If so means if that is the case. So replaces the whole question.
why.es: If so significa si es así. So reemplaza toda la pregunta.

it.en: “If it, send it” is not correct; so replaces the question.
it.es: «If it, send it» no es correcto; so reemplaza la pregunta.

then.en: “If then, send it” is not correct; so replaces the question.
then.es: «If then, send it» no es correcto; so reemplaza la pregunta.

examples: Are you free? If so, come in.
Is he coming? If so, tell me.

tr.en: Is it ready? If so, send it to me.
tr.es: ¿Está listo? Si es así, mándamelo.

items.sentence: Do you want to tell me? I'd rather ___.

why.en: I would rather not is a polite refusal: not replaces the whole verb phrase.
why.es: I would rather not es un rechazo cortés: not reemplaza todo el verbo.

no.en: “I would rather no” is not correct; after rather comes not.
no.es: «I would rather no» no es correcto; después de rather va not.

don't.en: “I would rather do not” is not correct; after rather comes not.
don't.es: «I would rather do not» no es correcto; después de rather va not.

examples: I would rather not go.
He would rather not say.

tr.en: Do you want to tell me? I'd rather not.
tr.es: ¿Me quieres decir? Prefiero no hacerlo.

items.sentence: Ann and Eva came. The ___ is a nurse.

why.en: The former means the first of two things mentioned.
why.es: The former significa el primero de dos cosas mencionadas.

formal.en: Formal means official; to point back to the first one you need former.
formal.es: Formal significa oficial; para referirse al primero mencionado hace falta former.

forward.en: Forward means ahead; to point back to the first one you need former.
forward.es: Forward significa hacia adelante; para referirse al primero mencionado hace falta former.

examples: Tea or coffee? I like the former.
Rome and Paris are old; the former is bigger.

tr.en: Ann and Eva came. The former is a nurse.
tr.es: Ann y Eva vinieron. La primera es enfermera.

why.en: After than the verb be stays: than I am.
why.es: Después de than el verbo be se queda: than I am.

do.en: Do cannot replace the verb be; you need am.
do.es: Do no puede reemplazar al verbo be; hace falta am.

have.en: Have would mark the present perfect; in the comparison you need am.
have.es: Have marcaría el presente perfecto; en la comparación hace falta am.

examples: She is older than I am.
They are richer than we are.

tr.en: He is taller than I am.
tr.es: Él es más alto que yo.

items.sentence: 'Can you stay?' 'I'm afraid I'm not able ___.'

why.en: In place of a dropped infinitive the to stays: I wasn’t able to.
why.es: En lugar de un infinitivo omitido el to se queda: I wasn’t able to.

so.en: “I wasn’t able so” is not correct; you need to.
so.es: «I wasn’t able so» no es correcto; hace falta to.

it.en: “I wasn’t able it” is not correct; you need to.
it.es: «I wasn’t able it» no es correcto; hace falta to.

examples: I'd like to, but I can't.
She wanted to, but couldn't.

tr.en: 'Can you stay?' 'I'm afraid I'm not able to.'
tr.es: “¿Te puedes quedar?” “Me temo que no puedo”.

items.sentence: Some people like jazz and ___ prefer rock.

other.en: Other is an adjective; without a noun you need others.
other.es: Other es un adjetivo; sin sustantivo hace falta others.

another.en: Another is singular; prefer asks for a plural subject (others).
another.es: Another es singular; prefer pide un sujeto plural (others).

examples: Some ran and others walked.
Some agree and others do not.

tr.en: Some people like jazz and others prefer rock.
tr.es: A algunas personas les gusta el jazz y otras prefieren el rock.

items.sentence: I lost my pen, so I need to buy ___ one.

other.en: “Other one” is not correct in this meaning; you need another one.
other.es: «Other one» no es correcto en este sentido; hace falta another one.

others.en: “Others one” is not correct; others is plural, without a noun.
others.es: «Others one» no es correcto; others es plural, sin sustantivo.

examples: I need another one.
Give me another one.

tr.en: I lost my pen, so I need to buy another one.
tr.es: Perdí mi pluma, así que necesito comprar otra.

items.sentence: I did not call him, but I should ___.

why.en: After should the have stays and the repeated verb call is dropped.
why.es: Después de should se queda have y se omite el verbo repetido call.

has.en: “Should has” is not correct; after should comes have.
has.es: «Should has» no es correcto; después de should va have.

to.en: “Should to” is not correct; a modal takes no to.
to.es: «Should to» no es correcto; un modal no lleva to.

examples: He did not come, but he could have.
I did not ask, but I should have.

tr.en: I did not call him, but I should have.
tr.es: No lo llamé, pero debí haberlo hecho.

items.sentence: There is tea and coffee; I prefer the ___.

why.en: The latter means the second of two things mentioned.
why.es: The latter significa el segundo de dos cosas mencionadas.

later.en: Later means after; to point back to the second one you need latter.
later.es: Later significa después; para referirse al segundo mencionado hace falta latter.

lately.en: Lately means recently; to point back to the second one you need latter.
lately.es: Lately significa últimamente; para referirse al segundo mencionado hace falta latter.

examples: I know Ann and Eva; the latter is a nurse.
Tea or coffee? I like the latter.

tr.en: There is tea and coffee; I prefer the latter.
tr.es: Hay té y café; prefiero el segundo.

items.sentence: She ordered the soup, and I did the ___.

why.en: Do the same is a fixed phrase: to do the same thing.
why.es: Do the same es una expresión fija: hacer lo mismo.

equal.en: “Did the equal” is not correct; the fixed phrase is do the same.
equal.es: «Did the equal» no es correcto; la expresión fija es do the same.

alike.en: “Did the alike” is not correct; the fixed phrase is do the same.
alike.es: «Did the alike» no es correcto; la expresión fija es do the same.

examples: She left, and I did the same.
He paid, and we did the same.

tr.en: She ordered the soup, and I did the same.
tr.es: Ella pidió la sopa y yo hice lo mismo.

why.en: After a conjunction the subject and be can be dropped: when asked means when he was asked.
why.es: Después de una conjunción se pueden omitir el sujeto y be: when asked significa when he was asked.

asking.en: “When asking his name” is not correct; you need the passive meaning (asked).
asking.es: «When asking his name» no es correcto; hace falta el sentido pasivo (asked).

ask.en: “When ask his name” is not correct; you need a participle (asked).
ask.es: «When ask his name» no es correcto; hace falta un participio (asked).

examples: When asked, she said no.
If asked, I will help.

tr.en: When asked his name, he lied.
tr.es: Cuando le preguntaron su nombre, mintió.

items.sentence: I haven't finished, but my sister ___.

why.en: After the auxiliary the verb is dropped: my sister has.
why.es: Después del auxiliar el verbo se omite: my sister has.

does.en: Does is not the auxiliary of the present perfect; you need has.
does.es: Does no es el auxiliar del presente perfecto; hace falta has.

is.en: Is belongs to the verb be; the present perfect needs has.
is.es: Is pertenece al verbo be; el presente perfecto necesita has.

examples: I can't swim, but he can.
She didn't go, but I did.

tr.en: I haven't finished, but my sister has.
tr.es: Yo no he terminado, pero mi hermana sí.

items.sentence: You can stay if you want ___.

why.en: The to of the infinitive stays: if you want to.
why.es: El to del infinitivo se queda: if you want to.

it.en: “If you want it” has another meaning (“if you need it”); to stands for a dropped verb.
it.es: «If you want it» tiene otro significado («si lo quieres»); to representa un verbo omitido.

so.en: “If you want so” is not correct; you need to.
so.es: «If you want so» no es correcto; hace falta to.

examples: Come if you like to.
I will if you want me to.

tr.en: You can stay if you want to.
tr.es: Te puedes quedar si quieres.

items.sentence: He asked me to leave, and I did ___.

why.en: A formal substitute: I did so.
why.es: Un sustituto formal: I did so.

such.en: “I did such” is not correct; you need so.
such.es: «I did such» no es correcto; hace falta so.

as.en: “I did as” is not correct in this structure; you need so.
as.es: «I did as» no es correcto en esta estructura; hace falta so.

examples: She asked me to stay, and I did so.
They told him to go, and he did so.

tr.en: He asked me to leave, and I did so.
tr.es: Me pidió que me fuera y así lo hice.

items.sentence: 'Are you coming?' 'I'd love ___, but I'm busy.'

why.en: The to of the infinitive stays: I’d love to.
why.es: El to del infinitivo se queda: I’d love to.

so.en: “I’d love so” is not correct; you need to.
so.es: «I’d love so» no es correcto; hace falta to.

too.en: “I’d love too” is not correct; you need to (too is another word).
too.es: «I’d love too» no es correcto; hace falta to (too es otra palabra).

examples: I'd like to.
I'd love to.

tr.en: 'Are you coming?' 'I'd love to, but I'm busy.'
tr.es: “¿Vienes?” “Me encantaría, pero estoy ocupado”.

items.sentence: I wouldn't accept it, and nor ___ any sensible person.

why.en: After nor the word order is inverted: nor would + subject.
why.es: Después de nor el orden se invierte: nor would + sujeto.

accepts.en: “Nor accepts any sensible person” is not correct; an auxiliary must come before the subject.
accepts.es: «Nor accepts any sensible person» no es correcto; hace falta un auxiliar antes del sujeto.

accept.en: “Nor accept any sensible person” is not correct; an auxiliary must come before the subject.
accept.es: «Nor accept any sensible person» no es correcto; hace falta un auxiliar antes del sujeto.

examples: He will not go, nor will I.
I do not agree, nor does she.

tr.en: I wouldn't accept it, and nor would any sensible person.
tr.es: Yo no lo aceptaría, ni tampoco ninguna persona sensata.
